paper.title_en: Background particle response of CMS GEM detectors with Run 3 data and simulation
paper.abstract_en: The upgrade of the High-Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC) will boost the instantaneous luminosity to 5–7 × 10<sup loc="post">34</sup> cm<sup loc="post">−2</sup>s<sup loc="post">−1</sup>, increasing particle fluxes in the forward region of the CMS detector. High particle fluxes can damage electronics and induce spurious signals. This study focuses on the GE1/1 triple-GEM detector’s sensitivity to both neutral and charged background particles, performed using FLUKA and GEANT4 simulations. FLUKA provides a comprehensive description of the radiation field around the GE1/1 chambers across a broad energy spectrum. GEANT4 delivers complementary insight into the detector response based on realistic geometry, materials, and interaction processes. The results show how the detector’s sensitivity changes with particle energy and incident angle, and how different configurations affect its performance. The article also includes comparisons with CMS Run 3 data, providing valuable guidance for optimizing GEM operation under HL-LHC conditions. This approach can be extended to other forward detectors like ME0 during the HL-LHC era. •FLUKA simulations for radiation environment studies.•GEANT4 simulations for GE1/1 geometry and sensitivity analysis.•Hit-rate calculation and comparison with Run 3 data.
